headlines.summary: 국민의힘 소득세법 일부 개정안 발의 주식·디지털자산 간 형평성 논란 확산 해외·DEX 등 과세 사각지대 발생 우려 재경부 “소득에 과세 원칙…논란 파악” 내년부터 개인투자자의 디지털자산 양도차익에 과세가 시행되는 가운데 야당이 이를 폐지하는 법안을 추진한다. 금융투자소득세가 폐지된 상황에서 주식과 디지털자산 간 과세 체계 형평성에 문제가 있다는 이유에서다.

key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Goo Yoon-chul: Price Hikes Inevitable with Price Ceiling Adjustment, Fuel Tax Cut Needed
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Goo Yoon-chul stated that adjusting the price ceiling system would inevitably lead to price increases, advocating for fuel tax cuts to alleviate public burden. He also announced plans to submit a 'war supplementary budget' by month-end to support ordinary citizens and small businesses, while promoting FX market stabilization laws and expanding policy financing.

key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Goo Yoon-chul Highlights Soaring Diesel Prices, Calls for Fuel Tax Cuts
key_headlines.summary: During a Cabinet meeting chaired by President Lee Jae-myung, Deputy Prime Minister Goo Yoon-chul emphasized the particularly high diesel prices and called for fuel tax cuts to minimize public burden amidst surging oil prices and exchange rates due to the Middle East situation. The 'FX Market Stabilization 3 Laws' are expected to be processed this month to address market volatility.

key_headlines.title: President Lee Jae-myung Orders Emergency Response to Middle East War, Vows Action Against Oil Price Collusion
key_headlines.summary: President Lee Jae-myung instructed the activation of an emergency response system for the Middle East conflict and pledged severe punishment for any collusion in oil prices. He also reiterated the need for swift processing of a 'war supplementary budget' to mitigate the impact of the prolonged conflict.

key_headlines.title: Public Sector Strengthens Mandatory 5-Day Car Rationing, Private Sector Encouraged Voluntarily
key_headlines.summary: The government is enhancing the mandatory 5-day car rationing system for 1.5 million public sector employees, imposing disciplinary action for repeat violations, aiming to save 3,000 barrels of oil daily. While voluntary for the private sector, public institutions and large corporations are encouraged to adjust commuting times to further conserve energy.

key_headlines.title: Korea's Effective Property Tax Rate Half of OECD Average, But Average Relative to GDP
key_headlines.summary: Korea's effective property tax rate is around 0.15%, which is about half the OECD average, partly influenced by previous tax burden reduction measures. However, when assessed as a burden relative to GDP, Korea's property tax level is considered average compared to international standards.

sections.Hot Economy News: The Korean government is actively responding to the escalating Middle East conflict, which has led to surging oil prices and exchange rates. Deputy Prime Minister Goo Yoon-chul announced plans for a 'war supplementary budget' by month-end to support vulnerable populations and small businesses, alongside implementing fuel tax cuts and expanding policy financing. President Lee Jae-my-ung called for an emergency response system and vowed to punish oil price collusion. Additionally, the public sector is tightening its 5-day car rationing to conserve energy, while property tax rates are reported to be half the OECD average in effective terms, though average relative to GDP.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Producer prices in Korea have risen for six consecutive months, with the index reaching its highest in 19 months, largely driven by surging international oil prices due to the US-Iran conflict. Key components like coal and petroleum products, particularly diesel (7.4%) and naphtha (9%), saw significant increases. The Bank of Korea anticipates that this will lead to increased inflationary pressure on consumer prices, especially as oil and exchange rates continue to climb. Globally, the ongoing Iran war is causing economic slowdown and inflation, as evidenced by significant drops in March's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) across major economies like the Eurozone, Australia, and India.
sections.Financial Markets: Korean financial markets experienced high volatility amidst a 'triple whammy' of surging oil prices, rising exchange rates, and concerns over US interest rate hikes due to the Middle East conflict. The KOSPI index sharply dropped over 6% on one day, triggering a sell-side circuit breaker (sidecar), as foreign investors offloaded shares, though individual investors bought a record amount. The next day, the market saw an unstable rebound, with KOSPI and KOSDAQ initially rising on hopes of US-Iran negotiations but paring gains and even briefly turning negative, indicating persistent geopolitical uncertainty. This market instability has also weighed on treasury bond yields, surpassing the perceived intervention threshold for the Bank of Korea.
sections.Industry & Technology: While the top 500 Korean companies saw a 24% increase in operating profit, this growth drops to only 7% excluding the semiconductor sector. Semiconductor and robot stocks are considered undervalued by experts, who recommend staggered buying during market dips. K-battery companies are responding to the electric vehicle demand slowdown by diversifying business into Energy Storage Systems (ESS) and non-EV sectors like robotics, focusing on profitability. Investment opportunities are emerging for AI semiconductor companies, attracting interest from 'National Growth Funds' and PEFs.
sections.Real Estate: President Lee Jae-myung emphasized the need for housing price stability, stating that 'neglecting real estate speculation will ruin the country,' and called for stricter measures. Meanwhile, Seoul's rental market is facing an 'impasse,' with a rapid decrease in available monthly rent properties across most districts. A persistent debate regarding real estate statistics continues, as official government data (Korea Real Estate Board) shows a significantly lower apartment price increase (0.05%) compared to private sector data (KB, 0.31%), highlighting potential discrepancies. Additionally, LH is recruiting residents for 9,120 leasehold housing units for newlywed, newborn, and multi-child families from March 24th to December 31st.
sections.International Economy: The US-Israel-Iran conflict continues to dominate global economic discussions, with reports suggesting European countries are providing significant, albeit undeclared, support to US military operations despite public rhetoric. The US Federal Reserve Chairman Powell's case regarding potential pressure for rate cuts or resignation was deemed insufficient by a US prosecutor, who will appeal the judge's decision. Meanwhile, Europe and Australia signed an FTA, aiming to eliminate 99% of tariffs, which is expected to boost Australia's economy by AUD 10 billion annually and stabilize global supply chains for critical minerals. Concerns over Trump's '48-hour ultimatum' on the conflict are causing oil price fluctuations and gold price drops, while expectations for US interest rate cuts this year are virtually disappearing, with some even mentioning a potential hike in April.
sections.AI & Economy: The Maeil Business Newspaper, celebrating its 60th anniversary, proposed that Korea adopt 'AI native nation' as a new growth strategy, emphasizing the need for policy and regulatory changes to foster an era where AI is like a mother tongue. There's a push to open national infrastructure, such as Busan Port, as 'regulation-free zones' for AI experimentation to secure competitiveness in Physical AI, including robotics and autonomous driving. Gwangju's Advanced 3rd District is also positioning itself as Korea's AI capital, aiming for an integrated AI industry, research, and residential complex. Political leaders from both ruling and opposition parties have expressed commitment to supporting Korea's leap to an AI powerhouse through legislative measures and policy support, including a proposal to provide every citizen with a monthly AI service subscription card.
sections.Others: The domestic ETN market showed rapid shifts, with top-performing ETNs moving from inverse silver to leveraged positions in a single day following Trump's shift from 'total devastation' threats to 'military attack suspension' regarding Iran. Ulsan City is providing 10 billion won in management stabilization funds to small and medium-sized enterprises affected by trade conditions like US tariff adjustments or exchange rate fluctuations, targeting companies with over 20% of total sales from exports or imports. Park Hong-geun was confirmed as the Minister of Planning and Budget, with his appointment approved by President Lee Jae-myung. A proposal was made to support the public with AI subscription cards and foster 'AI companies' to aid small businesses. Meanwhile, US memory chip stocks like Micron and SanDisk showed weakness despite a general rebound in the New York market driven by hopes of an end to the US-Iran conflict.
